topics.text: Movement of materials and starch testing

points.text: Green plants use light energy to make glucose; carbon dioxide and water are the raw materials, and glucose and oxygen are the products.
Chlorophyll is the green pigment in chloroplasts and absorbs the light energy needed for photosynthesis.
Water enters through the roots, while carbon dioxide enters leaves through openings called stomata. Oxygen is released from the leaves.
Plants can use glucose in respiration to release energy, or convert some glucose into starch for storage.
Add iodine solution to test a leaf for starch. Iodine changes from brown to blue-black when starch is present.

Light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration, and temperature can each limit the rate of photosynthesis. Increasing light intensity will not keep raising the rate if another factor, such as carbon dioxide, becomes limiting.

are carbon dioxide and water. The products are glucose and oxygen. Chlorophyll is the green pigment found in chloroplasts. It absorbs the
light energy needed for photosynthesis. Water enters a plant through its roots. Carbon dioxide enters leaves through small openings called stomata. Oxygen is
released from the leaves. A plant can use glucose and respiration to release energy. It can also convert some glucose into starch
for storage. To test the leaf for starch, add iodine solution. Iodine changes from brown to blue-black when starch is present. Light intensity,
